variables.policy_prompt_for_subgoal: The episode starts with the first letter of demo_moves. At every decision step, first update the memory as instructed (demo_moves from the demonstration at the first step, legs_done = carried-in legs_done + 1 at later steps, 0 at the first), then issue the subgoal demo_moves[legs_done] (zero-based). So at the first decision step issue demo_moves[0], at the second demo_moves[1], and so on. No option needs a point. The letters mean: A = move to the nearest left target (larger x) passing on the backward side (smaller y) of the stick; B = nearest right target (smaller x) passing on the forward side (larger y); C = nearest left target passing on the forward side; D = nearest right target passing on the backward side. If legs_done is beyond the end of demo_moves, or demo_moves is missing, re-derive what you can: if the demonstration is visible, rebuild the list from it; otherwise repeat the last letter in demo_moves, and if there is none, issue A.

fields.name: demo_moves
fields.description: If the memory carried in is empty (first decision step), read the DEMONSTRATION STEPS and write one menu letter per leg, in order. First fix the target slots from the first demonstration frame (the highlighted target plus every listed target; slots are spaced roughly 30 px or more apart in x). Then walk through the demonstration frames and, at every frame, assign the highlighted target to the nearest slot; every frame where the highlighted target is assigned to a different slot than in the previous frame ends one leg and starts the next, so the number of letters is exactly the number of such slot changes. A slot change always shows as a jump of tens of pixels to where a previously non-highlighted target sat. If the highlighted position is within a few pixels (under about 10 px) of the previous frame's highlighted position, it is the same target with coordinate jitter and nothing has changed; do not count it. Count a change even when the gripper returns to a target it already visited, even when the leg lasts only a few frames, and even when the change appears only in the very last demonstration frame; a visited target means a visited slot. A frame with two targets highlighted at once is the change frame: the newly highlighted target is the new one. For each leg: new target x smaller than the previous target x means RIGHT, larger means LEFT. The leg's frames are the frames AFTER its opening frame and BEFORE its closing change frame whose single highlighted target is the leg's starting target. For the first leg the opening frame is the very first demonstration frame, so its frames are the second frame onward until the first change. Never use frames at or after the closing change frame; those belong to the next leg and are often on the opposite side of the stick. The reference stick is the one cube whose x lies between the x of the starting target and the x of the new target. In each of the leg's frames compare gripper y with that cube's y in the same frame (the cube may shift slightly when brushed): gripper y smaller than the cube's y means it passed the BACKWARD side, larger means FORWARD. Do not compare the gripper with the new target's y and do not let the gripper's movement in the following leg decide the side. LEFT+backward=A, RIGHT+forward=B, LEFT+forward=C, RIGHT+backward=D. At every later step copy the list carried in unchanged. Write the list single-quoted with comma and space between letters, never with double quotes. e.g. ['A', 'B', 'A', 'D']
fields.annotation: The ordered list of menu letters, one per leg of the demonstration video, written at the first decision step and copied unchanged at every later step. A leg runs from one highlighted target to the moment a different target becomes highlighted (the gripper has reached the next target). Count one leg at EVERY change of the highlighted target: the number of letters equals the number of highlight changes in the demonstration, including legs that return to a target already visited, legs lasting only a few frames, and a change that appears only in the last demonstration frame; never merge or skip a leg because the gripper comes back to where it was. A frame showing two targets highlighted at once is the change frame: the leg ends there and the next leg starts there, the newly highlighted target being the new one. Targets are identified by slot, not by exact coordinates: the set of target slots is fixed for the episode (the slots are spaced roughly 30 px or more apart in x), and each frame's highlighted target is whichever slot it is nearest to. The highlighted target has changed only when it is assigned to a different slot than in the previous frame, which shows as a jump of tens of pixels to where a non-highlighted target sat; a highlighted position within a few pixels (under about 10 px) of the previous frame's highlighted position is the same target with coordinate jitter and does not end a leg. Letter for a leg: compare the x of the new target with the x of the previous target; smaller x is RIGHT, larger x is LEFT. Then take the leg's frames: exactly the demonstration frames whose single highlighted target is the leg's starting target, after the frame where that target first became highlighted (for the first leg that opening frame is the very first demonstration frame, so its frames run from the second frame up to the first change) and before the first frame in which the next target appears highlighted (a two-target frame is that closing frame and is excluded). Frames at or after the closing change frame belong to the following leg, never to this one. The reference stick is the one cube whose x lies between the x of the starting target and the x of the new target. In each of the leg's frames compare the gripper's y with that cube's y in the same frame (the cube may shift a few pixels when brushed): gripper y smaller than the cube's y means it passed the backward side, larger the forward side. The gripper's y relative to the new target and its travel in the next leg are irrelevant. LEFT+backward=A, RIGHT+forward=B, LEFT+forward=C, RIGHT+backward=D. The list has as many letters as legs in the demonstration, and it equals the sequence of recorded subgoals of the episode. Written as a single-quoted list, comma and space between letters, never double quotes. e.g. ['A', 'B', 'A', 'D']

fields.name: legs_done

  Holds the ordered list of menu letters, one per leg of the demonstration, written at the first decision step and copied unchanged afterwards; written as a Python-style list with single quotes, e.g. ['D', 'A', 'D', 'C', 'D', 'A', 'A']. The failure: a demonstration in which the gripper shuttles back and forth several times between the same two neighbouring targets (highlight going 108->81->108->81->108->81->108->138) was annotated with seven letters, but a policy reading the same video wrote only five, dropping the short return legs; the subgoal it chose was still right, so this breaks PREDICTABILITY of demo_moves. The rule must say explicitly: a leg is counted at EVERY change of the highlighted target, so the number of letters equals the number of highlight changes in the demonstration, including legs that return to a target already visited and legs of only a few frames; never merge or skip a leg because the gripper comes back to where it was. A frame that shows two targets highlighted at once is the frame at which the new target becomes highlighted: the leg ends there and the next leg starts there. The last demonstration frame may itself show the final highlight change and that change still counts as a leg. For the side letter, use the gripper frames strictly between the two highlight changes of that leg and compare their y with the y of the stick lying between the two targets. The list equals the recorded subgoal sequence of the episode, one letter per decision step.

First walk through the demonstration frames and list the highlighted target at every frame; every frame where the highlighted target differs from the previous frame's ends one leg and starts the next, so the number of letters is exactly the number of such changes. Count a change even when the gripper returns to a target it already visited, even when the leg lasts only a few frames, and even when the change appears only in the very last demonstration frame. A frame with two targets highlighted at once is the change frame: the newly highlighted target is the new one. For each leg: new target x smaller than the previous target x means RIGHT, larger means LEFT. Gripper y in the frames strictly between the two change frames of the leg smaller than the y of the stick (cube) between the two targets means it passed the BACKWARD side, larger means FORWARD. LEFT+backward=A, RIGHT+forward=B, LEFT+forward=C, RIGHT+backward=D. At every later step copy the list carried in unchanged. Write the list single-quoted with comma and space between letters, never with double quotes. e.g. ['A', 'B', 'A', 'D']
fields.annotation: The ordered list of menu letters, one per leg of the demonstration video, written at the first decision step and copied unchanged at every later step. A leg runs from one highlighted target to the moment a different target becomes highlighted (the gripper has reached the next target). Count one leg at EVERY change of the highlighted target: the number of letters equals the number of highlight changes in the demonstration, including legs that return to a target already visited, legs lasting only a few frames, and a change that appears only in the last demonstration frame; never merge or skip a leg because the gripper comes back to where it was. A frame showing two targets highlighted at once is the change frame: the leg ends there and the next leg starts there, the newly highlighted target being the new one. Letter for a leg: compare the x of the new target with the x of the previous target; smaller x is RIGHT, larger x is LEFT. Then look at the gripper's y in the frames strictly between the two highlight changes of that leg against the y of the stick (cube) it passed between the two targets: smaller y means it passed the backward side, larger y the forward side. LEFT+backward=A, RIGHT+forward=B, LEFT+forward=C, RIGHT+backward=D. The list has as many letters as legs in the demonstration, and it equals the sequence of recorded subgoals of the episode. Written as a single-quoted list, comma and space between letters, never double quotes. e.g. ['A', 'B', 'A', 'D']

fields.name: legs_done
fields.description: Write 0 if the memory carried in is empty (first decision step). Otherwise write the carried-in legs_done plus 1, because every decision step after the first shows one completed execution leg (the gripper moved and a different target became highlighted). e.g. 1
fields.annotation: Number of execution legs the robot has completed so far, i.e. the index of the decision step counting from zero: 0 at the first decision step, 1 at the second, 2 at the third, and so on. It is the index into demo_moves of the subgoal to issue now. e.g. 1

variables.policy_prompt_for_subgoal: The episode starts with the first letter of demo_moves. At every decision step, first update the memory as instructed (demo_moves from the demonstration at the first step, legs_done = carried-in legs_done + 1 at later steps, 0 at the first), then issue the subgoal demo_moves[legs_done] (zero-based). So at the first decision step issue demo_moves[0], at the second demo_moves[1], and so on. No option needs a point. The letters mean: A = move to the nearest left target (larger x) passing on the backward side (smaller y) of the stick; B = nearest right target (smaller x) passing on the forward side (larger y); C = nearest left target passing on the forward side; D = nearest right target passing on the backward side. If legs_done is beyond the end of demo_moves, or demo_moves is missing, re-derive what you can: if the demonstration is visible, rebuild the list from it; otherwise repeat the last letter in demo_moves, and if there is none, issue A.

fields.name: demo_moves
fields.description: If the memory carried in is empty (first decision step), read the DEMONSTRATION STEPS and write one menu letter per leg, in order. First walk through the demonstration frames and list the highlighted target at every frame; every frame where the highlighted target differs from the previous frame's ends one leg and starts the next, so the number of letters is exactly the number of such changes. Count a change even when the gripper returns to a target it already visited, even when the leg lasts only a few frames, and even when the change appears only in the very last demonstration frame. A frame with two targets highlighted at once is the change frame: the newly highlighted target is the new one. For each leg: new target x smaller than the previous target x means RIGHT, larger means LEFT. The leg's frames are the frames AFTER its opening frame and BEFORE its closing change frame whose single highlighted target is the leg's starting target. For the first leg the opening frame is the very first demonstration frame, so its frames are the second frame onward until the first change. Never use frames at or after the closing change frame; those belong to the next leg and are often on the opposite side of the stick. The reference stick is the one cube whose x lies between the x of the starting target and the x of the new target. In each of the leg's frames compare gripper y with that cube's y in the same frame (the cube may shift slightly when brushed): gripper y smaller than the cube's y means it passed the BACKWARD side, larger means FORWARD. Do not compare the gripper with the new target's y and do not let the gripper's movement in the following leg decide the side. LEFT+backward=A, RIGHT+forward=B, LEFT+forward=C, RIGHT+backward=D. At every later step copy the list carried in unchanged. Write the list single-quoted with comma and space between letters, never with double quotes. e.g. ['A', 'B', 'A', 'D']
fields.annotation: The ordered list of menu letters, one per leg of the demonstration video, written at the first decision step and copied unchanged at every later step. A leg runs from one highlighted target to the moment a different target becomes highlighted (the gripper has reached the next target). In each of the leg's frames compare the gripper's y with that cube's y in the same frame (the cube may shift a few pixels when brushed): gripper y smaller than the cube's y means it passed the backward side, larger the forward side. The gripper's y relative to the new target and its travel in the next leg are irrelevant. LEFT+backward=A, RIGHT+forward=B, LEFT+forward=C, RIGHT+backward=D. The list has as many letters as legs in the demonstration, and it equals the sequence of recorded subgoals of the episode. Written as a single-quoted list, comma and space between letters, never double quotes. e.g. ['A', 'B', 'A', 'D']

fields.name: demo_moves
fields.description: If the memory carried in is empty (first decision step), read the DEMONSTRATION STEPS and write one menu letter per leg, in order. First fix the target slots from the first demonstration frame (the highlighted target plus every listed target; slots are spaced roughly 30 px or more apart in x). Then walk through the demonstration frames and, at every frame, assign the highlighted target to the nearest slot; every frame where the highlighted target is assigned to a different slot than in the previous frame ends one leg and starts the next, so the number of letters is exactly the number of such slot changes. A slot change always shows as a jump of tens of pixels to where a previously non-highlighted target sat. If the highlighted position is within a few pixels (under about 10 px) of the previous frame's highlighted position, it is the same target with coordinate jitter and nothing has changed; do not count it. Count a change even when the gripper returns to a target it already visited, even when the leg lasts only a few frames, and even when the change appears only in the very last demonstration frame; a visited target means a visited slot. A frame with two targets highlighted at once is the change frame: the newly highlighted target is the new one. For each leg: new target x smaller than the previous target x means RIGHT, larger means LEFT. The leg's frames are the frames AFTER its opening frame and BEFORE its closing change frame whose single highlighted target is the leg's starting target. For the first leg the opening frame is the very first demonstration frame, so its frames are the second frame onward until the first change. Never use frames at or after the closing change frame; those belong to the next leg and are often on the opposite side of the stick. The reference stick is the one cube whose x lies between the x of the starting target and the x of the new target. In each of the leg's frames compare gripper y with that cube's y in the same frame (the cube may shift slightly when brushed): gripper y smaller than the cube's y means it passed the BACKWARD side, larger means FORWARD. Do not compare the gripper with the new target's y and do not let the gripper's movement in the following leg decide the side. LEFT+backward=A, RIGHT+forward=B, LEFT+forward=C, RIGHT+backward=D. At every later step copy the list carried in unchanged. Write the list single-quoted with comma and space between letters, never with double quotes. e.g. ['A', 'B', 'A', 'D']
fields.annotation: The ordered list of menu letters, one per leg of the demonstration video, written at the first decision step and copied unchanged at every later step. A leg runs from one highlighted target to the moment a different target becomes highlighted (the gripper has reached the next target). Count one leg at EVERY change of the highlighted target: the number of letters equals the number of highlight changes in the demonstration, including legs that return to a target already visited, legs lasting only a few frames, and a change that appears only in the last demonstration frame; never merge or skip a leg because the gripper comes back to where it was. A frame showing two targets highlighted at once is the change frame: the leg ends there and the next leg starts there, the newly highlighted target being the new one. Targets are identified by slot, not by exact coordinates: the set of target slots is fixed for the episode (the slots are spaced roughly 30 px or more apart in x), and each frame's highlighted target is whichever slot it is nearest to. The highlighted target has changed only when it is assigned to a different slot than in the previous frame, which shows as a jump of tens of pixels to where a non-highlighted target sat; a highlighted position within a few pixels (under about 10 px) of the previous frame's highlighted position is the same target with coordinate jitter and does not end a leg. Frames at or after the closing change frame belong to the following leg, never to this one. The reference stick is the one cube whose x lies between the x of the starting target and the x of the new target.
